response.root_cause: backend/app/services/transcriptions.py:93 (added by commit c65a326, 'log the real-time factor') computes `elapsed_ms / 1000 / result.duration_seconds` and only guards against None. When the provider reports a duration of 0.0, this raises ZeroDivisionError and the request returns 500 (status=server_error). Only very short uploads trigger it. The fake provider computes the duration as round(size / 16000, 2), so any file under about 80 bytes gets 0.0 s. Every failing trace has echonotes.audio.size_bytes=44, which is an empty WAV header. Normal-length uploads have a positive duration and succeed.

response.summary: INC-20261111-052713: about 40% of transcriptions failed with HTTP 500 after commit c65a326 was deployed. That commit added a real-time-factor log field. It divides by the audio duration the provider reports and only checks for None, so very short clips with a reported duration of 0.0 s (here, 44-byte empty WAV files) raised ZeroDivisionError. The fix changes the guard to a truthiness check: the factor is logged only when the duration is positive, and the transcript is still created. A new unit test uploads a 44-byte WAV through the fake provider and expects 201. It failed with ZeroDivisionError before the fix and passes after. All 457 unit tests pass, and ruff check and ruff format --check are clean. The log fields are unchanged apart from leaving out realtime_factor in that case. No transcript text, titles or filenames are logged.
